Em.bar_b_note: Site-specific aftermath story (open cage, fallen banner, smoking collapsed tent, revealed rune stone) carries side A, but smeared low-detail ground textures, flat noon light and sparse floating props sink both sides well below Palworld density and Valheim atmosphere.

Ai.bar_b_note: Brooktail is a Palworld-class hero model, but a bare blurry meadow, puff-ball spray VFX and a HUD that frames the fighters keep it from reading as the same finish.

Fo.bar_b_note: A warm, appealing, clearly identifiable elder villager with readable eyes and a natural olive/cream/leather palette carries it, though he sits on a void stage with flat fill light rather than Valheim-class rim and grade.

Fj.bar_b_note: Side B frames both fighters cleanly on a grass slope, but tiny distant creatures, white puff clouds and yellow ring icons over the struck creature, and side A's fence-and-banner occlusion sink it.

Ay.bar_b_note: Voltarach's copper-and-blue silhouette is on-board, but a murky brown-grey forest with no purple storm sky or lightning, flat magenta floor shapes, a near-invisible player creature, a HUD covering much of each frame and (side A) trunk/canopy blackouts sink it.

Pm.bar_b_note: Saturated blue-and-gold aquatic drake with a clear spined silhouette reads at a shipping-creature finish, held back by a back height only about level with the 1.80 m trainer, A's collapsed faint-end heap and B's floating faint-mid pose.

Uz.bar_b_note: Torch-lit stone hall has real Valheim-like warmth and two large readable creatures, but the player's Ripplet vanishing in side A and cotton-ball dust trails covering both fighters keep it short of shipping finish.

Ys.bar_b_note: Aeriex and the castle arena give a strong landmark backdrop and B's dusk/rain grade adds mood, but puff rings, speed-line streaks, A's white impact disc and an empty flat arena floor read as prototype rather than Palworld finish.

top_changes.change: Replace the shared combat VFX language (white puff-ball trails, white impact discs, yellow ring icons, flat magenta floor triangles/rings) with grounded real-object effects: water splash and spray sheets, kicked stones/dust at the struck creature's feet, lightning arcs, plus body-driven tell anticipation so tells no longer depend on HUD text.

Fight camera and framing rules: always keep the player's creature on screen, solid and at readable size, push the camera past occluders (Fj A fence/banners, Ay A trunks and canopy), and shrink/realign HUD panels so they never sit over the fighters (Ay especially).

Terrain and atmosphere pass: replace smeared low-res ground textures with detailed grass/dirt materials and clumped vegetation (Em, Ai, Fj), and give Stormwood its purple storm sky, rim light and white-violet lightning so Ay separates from mud-brown.
